column1: # ComputerBase — AMD Radeon RX 9070 (XT) im Test, Gaming-Benchmarks.
# Rasteriser charts, article pages 3, 4 and 5, at 2.560 × 1.440 and 3.840 × 2.160.
# THE WHOLE RASTERISER PARCOURS, not a sample. The file this replaces took four
# of the review's 23 games, to respect a per-source concentration cap that was
# removed on 2026-08-10 and replaced by measure-and-report. Taking the rest also
# dilutes Notebookcheck, which had grown to 87.7% of the corpus.
# Figures read from each bar's data-value attribute — transcribed, never
# estimated off an image. Average and P1 (their 1% percentile). Extracted by
# src/lib/perfEngine/computerbase.js, whose output was verified by re-deriving
# the 160 rows previously committed from this review: all 160 matched exactly.
# Presets are ComputerBase's own, read per game off the settings table on the
# inferred. Upscaling is per CHART, because it varies by resolution within one
# game, and it is now part of the cell key.
# NOT imported from this review, on purpose:
#   - the 3.440 × 1.440 charts: 21:9 ultrawide is 34% more pixels than 16:9 at
#     the same height, and RESOLUTIONS has no slot for it. Filing it under
#     1440p would assert a pixel count nobody measured.
#   - every RAY-TRACED chart. RT is a materially different setting and the cell
#     key has no slot for it, so filing it beside its rasteriser twin would mix
#     two measurements. Indiana Jones und der große Kreis and Star Wars Outlaws
#     are measured ONLY with RT, so this review yields nothing for them.
#   - Lego: Horizon Adventures: run at "70 % TSR", which is not one of the
#     named UPSCALING modes. Calling it Quality (66.7%) would misstate it.
#   - the "Full HD:" settings noted in the table: 1080p is not imported here.
#   - any cell with an average but no P1 lands with no low, never an invented one.
